content.value_statement: Architecture decisions often lose context after implementation. This skill helps teams create ADRs with clear context, options, consequences, and review practices.
actual_capabilities: Provides standard, lightweight, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style ADR formats.
Explains when to write an ADR and when a decision does not need one.
Structures decision drivers, considered options, rationale, consequences, risks, and references.
Shows ADR lifecycle states such as proposed, accepted, deprecated, superseded, and rejected.
Includes guidance for ADR directories, indexes, review checklists, and adr-tools workflows.
limitations: Does not decide architecture choices without project context and stakeholder input.
Does not validate product metrics, benchmark data, or compliance requirements.
Does not replace engineering review for high-risk security or infrastructure decisions.
Does not maintain files automatically unless the user asks for repository edits.

use_cases.title: Record a Platform Choice
use_cases.description: Create an ADR that compares options, states the selected technology, and documents trade-offs for future maintainers.

use_cases.title: Improve Decision Reviews
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to confirm context, alternatives, consequences, security impact, and implementation follow-up are covered.

use_cases.title: Organize an ADR Repository
use_cases.description: Set up a consistent ADR directory, index, statuses, and naming convention for a growing engineering team.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: document one clear decision with known context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an ADR for this decision: [decision]. Include status, context, options, decision, consequences, and related follow-up work.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Decision Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: evaluate several alternatives before the decision is final.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR that compares these options: [options]. Use decision drivers, pros and cons, risks, mitigations, and a recommended decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: strengthen a draft before team review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ADR draft for clarity, missing context, weak trade-offs, security impact, and implementation gaps: [draft]. Suggest concise revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an ADR Program
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: establish a repeatable decision process for a team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ADR workflow for our team. Include statuses, file naming, index structure, review rules, superseding rules, and guidance for when to write an ADR.

output_examples.input: Choose PostgreSQL as the primary database for an e-commerce platform.
output_examples.output: A structured ADR covering transaction needs, search requirements, considered databases, the PostgreSQL decision, expected benefits, operational costs, and related decisions.

output_examples.input: Review a draft ADR that proposes adopting TypeScript for a React codebase.
output_examples.output: A review noting missing decision drivers, unclear migration scope, incomplete risks, and suggested wording for consequences and rollout steps.

output_examples.input: Set up ADR practices for a team that has no decision log.
output_examples.output: A recommended ADR directory, naming pattern, lifecycle statuses, review checklist, and index format for consistent future decisions.

best_practices: Write ADRs before implementation starts so the decision can still be reviewed.
Keep each ADR focused on one decision with clear options and consequences.
Create new ADRs to supersede old decisions instead of rewriting accepted history.
anti_patterns: Using ADRs to document minor bug fixes or routine configuration changes.
Listing only the chosen option without rejected alternatives and trade-offs.
Accepting ADRs without owners, follow-up work, or links to related decisions.

faq.question: What is an Architecture Decision Record?
faq.answer: An ADR is a short document that records the context, decision, and consequences of an important technical choice.

faq.question: When should I write an ADR?
faq.answer: Write one for significant architecture, technology, integration, security, or process decisions that future teams need to understand.

faq.question: Can this skill review an existing ADR?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check whether the draft explains context, alternatives, risks, consequences, and implementation follow-up clearly.

faq.question: Does it support multiple ADR formats?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes standard MADR, lightweight, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style formats.

faq.question: Can it manage ADR files in a repository?
faq.answer: It can suggest directory structures, indexes, naming rules, and workflows. File changes require explicit user direction.

faq.question: Does an ADR replace technical review?
faq.answer: No. An ADR improves review quality, but stakeholders still need to validate feasibility, risk, cost, and compliance.
